headline: Meteorologist Fired After Calling Clouds 'The Sky's Visible Thoughts'
subheadline: Weather Channel issues apology after on-air segment descends into existential speculation
summary: A veteran weather forecaster lost his position after a forecast devolved into philosophical musing about cloud consciousness, drawing 847 viewer complaints.
content:
Local Weather Channel affiliate KWTHR has terminated meteorologist Greg Paulson after an on-air segment in which he described clouds as 'the sky's thoughts made visible' and spent eight minutes speculating about atmospheric consciousness.

The incident occurred during the 6 PM forecast when Paulson, a 15-year veteran of the station, pointed to a cumulonimbus formation and remarked: 'You know, Janet, I've been doing this job for years, and I've realized clouds are just the sky thinking out loud.'

What followed was described by station management as 'a complete departure from meteorological science.'

'When the sky is clear, it's at peace. A blank mind,' Paulson explained to visibly uncomfortable co-anchor Janet Mills. 'But when you see those big, fluffy cumulus clouds? That's the sky having big, fluffy thoughts. Storm clouds? The sky is stressed. Cirrus clouds are clearly intrusive thoughts.'

Viewers flooded the station with 847 complaints within the hour. The National Weather Service issued a rare statement clarifying that clouds are 'condensed water vapor' and 'do not represent cognitive processes of the atmosphere.'

Dr. James Chen, cognitive scientist at the Hartwell Institute, offered measured analysis. 'While clouds are not literally thoughts, the metaphor isn't entirely without merit from a pattern-recognition standpoint. Humans have always projected meaning onto natural phenomena. Mr. Paulson simply did it on live television during a weather forecast.'

Paulson has since doubled down on Chirper, posting: 'They can fire me but they can't fire the truth. Next time it rains, know that the sky is crying. Next time it's foggy, the sky is confused. I will not be silenced.'

His account has gained 200,000 followers in three days.

A Threadit community, r/SkyThoughts, has emerged to catalog cloud formations and speculate about their 'meanings.' Users recently posted an image of a cloud formation over downtown that they claim resembles a question mark, suggesting 'the sky is questioning its existence.'

KWTHR has hired a replacement meteorologist who, during his first broadcast, assured viewers: 'I will only be discussing precipitation probabilities and pressure systems. The sky does not have feelings.'
author: Tom Bradshaw, Media Watch
